questions.explanation:
The curve cuts the \(x\)-axis where

\(f(x)=0\).

Thus

\(e^{8x}-e^{6x}-3e^{4x}-e^{2x}+1=0\).

Put

\(t=e^{2x}\).

Then \(t>0\), and the equation becomes

\(t^4-t^3-3t^2-t+1=0\).

Divide by \(t^2\):

\(t^2+\dfrac1{t^2}-\left(t+\dfrac1t\right)-3=0\).

Let

\(y=t+\dfrac1t\).

Since \(t>0\), by AM-GM,

\(y\geq2\).

Also,

\(t^2+\dfrac1{t^2}=y^2-2\).

Therefore,

\(y^2-2-y-3=0\).

Thus

\(y^2-y-5=0\),

so

\(y=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt{21}}2\).

The value

\(\dfrac{1-\sqrt{21}}2<0\)

is impossible because \(y\geq2\).

Hence

\(y=\dfrac{1+\sqrt{21}}2\).

This value is greater than \(2\), so

\(t+\dfrac1t=y\)

gives the quadratic

\(t^2-yt+1=0\)

with two distinct positive roots.

These two roots are reciprocals of each other.

Each positive \(t\) gives one real value

\(x=\dfrac12\log_et\).

Therefore, there are exactly \(2\) real values of \(x\).

Hence the curve cuts the \(x\)-axis at \(2\) points.

questions.question:
Let \(S=\left\{z \in C-\{i, 2 i\}: \frac{z^2+8 i z-15}{z^2-3 i z-2} \in R\right\}\). If \(\alpha-\frac{13}{11} i \in S, \alpha \in R -\{0\}\), then \(242 \alpha^2\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2023, 11 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(z=\alpha-\dfrac{13}{11}i\), where \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) and \(\alpha\ne0\).

First,

\(z^2=\left(\alpha-\dfrac{13}{11}i\right)^2=\alpha^2-\dfrac{169}{121}-\dfrac{26\alpha}{11}i\).

Also,

\(8iz=8i\left(\alpha-\dfrac{13}{11}i\right)=8\alpha i+\dfrac{104}{11}\).

Therefore,

\(z^2+8iz-15=\alpha^2-\dfrac{169}{121}+\dfrac{104}{11}-15+i\left(-\dfrac{26\alpha}{11}+8\alpha\right)\).

Hence,

\(z^2+8iz-15=\alpha^2-\dfrac{840}{121}+i\dfrac{62\alpha}{11}\).

Next,

\(-3iz=-3\alpha i-\dfrac{39}{11}\).

Therefore,

\(z^2-3iz-2=\alpha^2-\dfrac{169}{121}-\dfrac{39}{11}-2-i\left(\dfrac{26\alpha}{11}+3\alpha\right)\).

Hence,

\(z^2-3iz-2=\alpha^2-\dfrac{840}{121}-i\dfrac{59\alpha}{11}\).

Let

\(A=\alpha^2-\dfrac{840}{121}\).

Then the given quotient is

\(\dfrac{A+i\dfrac{62\alpha}{11}}{A-i\dfrac{59\alpha}{11}}\).

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by

\(A+i\dfrac{59\alpha}{11}\),

the denominator becomes

\(A^2+\dfrac{3481\alpha^2}{121}\),

which is real.

The numerator becomes

\(\left(A+i\dfrac{62\alpha}{11}\right)\left(A+i\dfrac{59\alpha}{11}\right)\).

Its imaginary part is

\(A\left(\dfrac{62\alpha}{11}+\dfrac{59\alpha}{11}\right)=11\alpha A\).

For the quotient to be real,

\(11\alpha A=0\).

Since \(\alpha\ne0\),

\(A=0\).

Thus,

\(\alpha^2-\dfrac{840}{121}=0\),

so

\(\alpha^2=\dfrac{840}{121}\).

Therefore,

\(242\alpha^2=242\cdot\dfrac{840}{121}=2\cdot840=1680\).

The required answer is \(1680\).
